segments.text: This season finale centers on Claire trying to organize one perfect family portrait. She wants the whole extended family dressed in white and standing together on the staircase. To her, it isn’t just a picture.

segments.text: The children are growing up quickly, and she wants to capture the family as it is right now.

segments.text: Unfortunately, almost everything goes wrong before the photographer even arrives. A broken step is visible in the background, and Claire makes it much worse while trying to fix it herself.

segments.text: Meanwhile, Phil takes Alex to a Lakers game with Gloria and Manny. Claire calls him while he’s on television, but Phil ignores the call because he’s having fun. A few minutes later, the kiss cam lands on him and Gloria.

segments.text: They refuse to kiss at first, but the crowd starts booing, so Gloria quickly kisses him.

segments.text: Claire doesn’t actually see the kiss, but Phil thinks she does and spends the rest of the day feeling guilty. When he gets home, he keeps trying to explain himself, even though Claire is mainly angry that he ignored her call.

segments.text: Cameron has been hired to sing at a wedding, but Mitchell stays home with Lily because he hates making small talk with strangers. While Cameron is singing, a pigeon flies into their house.

segments.text: Luke also needs to interview Jay about life in the 1960s for a school project. Jay’s real stories are so ordinary that Luke keeps falling asleep, so Jay starts making things up.

segments.text: Soon, he’s claiming that his family’s barber shop served Martin Luther King Jr., the Kennedys, and even Elvis.

segments.text: Phil admits that Gloria kissed him, Cameron complains about Mitchell missing the wedding, and Claire becomes more desperate to make everyone look like a normal, happy family.

segments.text: Jay finally tells Claire that life isn’t perfect and throws mud at her. Within seconds, everyone joins in, and their clean white clothes are completely ruined.

segments.text: Strangely, that’s when the family finally relaxes. They take the picture covered in mud, laughing instead of posing. It isn’t the perfect portrait Claire planned, but later she realizes it’s a much better picture of what their family is really like.
